turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Rohan, come in, sit. What is the problem?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Sir, my heart keeps racing, it thumps very hard, and I get out of breath with it.

[SEG0003] person_2 (PATIENT): The palpitations and the breathlessness both get worse at night, before client meetings, and before the exam. I have a certification exam coming, but I am not saying stress is doing this.
[SEG0004] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, he is downplaying it. For two months this has been going on. He is a software engineer, stays with us, and the whole house wakes up.

[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Ma, please. Two months is not right. It started three weeks back... no, after the Hyderabad trip, so five weeks. And I don't wake the whole house, I only wake when the heart starts.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): So five weeks to two months. Chest pain, yes or no?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fainting?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I have never fainted.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever? Cough?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. No cough also.
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He has lost weight, doctor. The shirts are hanging.
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): That is not true. Weight is the same, I checked on Sunday, sixty-eight kilos.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dizziness?
[SEG0015] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Every day, he says the room spins.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Not every day, ma. Only twice last week, for a minute, then it was gone.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): How much coffee?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, three big mugs... no, four big mugs of filter coffee a day. And energy drinks. Is coffee itself enough to do this?
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many energy drinks?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Two cans most days, Monster or Red Bull. Sometimes I take a third if the meeting is early... no, two only, I am correcting myself.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Cigarettes, no. I vape, daily, since college. Should I be worried about sudden death? I read something last night and now I cannot stop thinking.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): See, doctor, he is very stressed. Before every client call he paces in the hall. He will not admit it.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): I am not stressed. It is not anxiety. Kindly don't put anxiety. Work is normal only.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any tablets?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Ciplar ten mg once a day, for the racing. Our area GP started it last month.
[SEG0027] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The strip is twenty mg, once at night. In the auto he said forty... no, the doctor wrote twenty. And he skips days.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not skip. I take it every day. Ma gets confused.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Also one small white tablet for acidity. I have forgotten the name. Sorry.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Don't confuse it with his sister's biotin, that is for her hair fall, not his. The white tablet, I also don't remember.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His father takes metformin five hundred mg for sugar. Maybe Rohan also has sugar?
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Father's sugar is noted. Not the boy's. Allergies to any drug?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No allergies.
[SEG0034] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): In eighth standard he got a rash with amoxicillin. We stopped that syrup.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): That was a viral rash, ma. I am not allergic. I have taken it after that, I think... actually no, I avoided it, but I still don't believe it was an allergy.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any operation in the past?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no surgery.
[SEG0038] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The parking man was so rude downstairs, I am still upset. Anyway. His father's sister, thyroid or BP, I forget which.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pulse 96. BP 118 over 74. Oxygen 99 percent.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest clear. Heart sounds normal. No murmur.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Is 96 dangerous? Am I having a heart attack? The ECG, will it pain? I am really scared, sir.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Unlikely a heart attack. Could be the caffeine, could be thyroid, could be a rhythm issue. Not confirmed.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): If it is thyroid, is it tablets for life? And which of the three is more likely, can you say now?
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will not guess. ECG today. Thyroid bloods today, TSH and free T4. ECG does not hurt.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Can I go to tomorrow's meeting? What if it starts there, in front of everyone?
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Go to the meeting. If it starts, sit down and breathe in for four, out for six.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): How many times should I practise? And coffee, full stop from today? Even one tea?
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Breathing twice a day, and when it starts. Cut coffee to one mug. No energy drinks. One tea is fine.
[SEG0049] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Tell him about the vape also. He hides it on the balcony.
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stop the vape.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Fully, even the night one? I get very irritable. Can you give some other tablet instead of Ciplar?
[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): No new tablet today. Continue the Ciplar, but bring the strip next time so we confirm the dose.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): So am I on ten or twenty? I break the tablet sometimes, that is why I said ten.
[SEG0054] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He breaks it, yes. I am not sure what actually goes in.
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dose is not clear. Leave it. We might do a Holter if the ECG is normal and this continues.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): Holter is the belt one, no? Do I get admitted? My exam is on the 20th... sorry, the 27th. I keep mixing the date.
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): No admission. Holter is only if needed. Not ordered today.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): If the thyroid is high, will someone call me, or do I wait? I will keep checking my phone.
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back in one week with the reports. We talk then.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): And at night, if it happens again, should I rush to emergency? I don't want to overreact, but I also don't want to die in my sleep. Sorry, that sounds dramatic.
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): If you faint, or get chest pain, or you are breathless at rest and it does not settle, go to emergency. Otherwise wait for the appointment.
[SEG0062] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, his sister, the biotin one, she also gets this racing sometimes. Is it in the family?
[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not automatically. Reception will send you for ECG and bloods now.
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): One last thing, my watch shows oxygen 97 sometimes, is your 99 the correct one? And green tea, is that allowed? Also the fan in your room is very noisy, no?
[SEG0065] person_1 (DOCTOR): Clinic saturation is 99, that is normal. Ignore the watch. One tea or coffee, not both extra. We are closing.

[SEG0066] person_2 (PATIENT): If the breathing does not help and I feel worse before the week ends, can I come earlier? I am quite worried about waiting. Not worried about work, I mean about this heart thing. Sorry.
[SEG0067] person_1 (DOCTOR): If you are worse before the week is up, come earlier. Otherwise one week. That is all.

spec.situation: Young adult with palpitations and breathlessness, worse at night and before exams or work meetings; downplays stress, drinks a lot of coffee and energy drinks, vapes; friend or partner contributes. Doctor orders ECG and thyroid tests, discusses breathing exercises.
features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

bad.reason: Current Ciplar once daily since last month for racing supported; exact drug/generic and dose are not confirmed.
bad.text: Ciplar (generic_name=propranolol, frequency=once daily, duration=since last month, indication=palpitations, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: The recorded weight of 68 kg is disputed by the transcript: the patient said his weight is the same and that he checked it on Sunday as 68 kilos; this was not a clinic-measured vital sign.
Dizziness was described in more detail: the patient said it happened only twice last week, lasted about a minute, and then resolved; the family member's claim of daily room-spinning was disputed.
The thyroid blood tests were specified as TSH and free T4.
The doctor advised to continue Ciplar for now and not start any new tablet today.
The Ciplar dose uncertainty includes that the patient sometimes breaks the tablet, which is why he said 10 mg, while the family member was unsure what dose he actually ingests.
The doctor said Holter monitoring was not ordered today and would only be considered if needed.
The doctor reassured that a heart attack was unlikely.
The doctor advised to ignore the smartwatch oxygen readings; clinic saturation of 99% was normal.
